newsitem.title: UK: Brazil 1996/97 sugar output seen at 15 mln t.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1996/97 sugar output seen at 15 mln t.

text.p: Brazil could produce as much as 15.0 million tonnes of sugar raw value in 1996/97 despite adverse weather conditions, up from the 13.59 million tonnes turned out in 1995/96, Czarnikow Sugar said on Thursday.
In its latest monthly report, Czarnikow said harvesting operations in the north-northeast (NNE) growing area had recovered into last month, following rains disrupting work in the fields.
Higher estimates in the centre-south (CS) put total cane output at 225 million tonnes, after the 220 million tonnes which had been expected previously.

"With CS production possibly rising to 11.14-11.40 million tonnes following these estimates and a NNE crop of around 3.6 million tonnes, it is now possibe that the national crop could rise to 15 million tonnes," Czarnikow said.
It added that a five percent gain in consumption was likely this season, which would indicate a demand of 8.45 million tonnes for 1996/97.
In its last monthly review, Czarnikow estimated 1996/97 Brazilian sugar output at 14.85 million tonnes. -- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
